title: Console Suggestions (beta): list + detail drawer UX (filters, comparison, risk/savings disclosure)
creator: Tessa Morgan
body:
Goal
Design the end-to-end UX for the new Redwood Console “Suggestions” view (beta): a Suggestions list/table and a detail drawer that clearly communicates (1) what to change, (2) expected savings with uncertainty, (3) risk level with concrete rationale, and (4) the basis/assumptions behind the estimate.

This ticket focuses on the list + detail drawer interaction model, filter patterns, and disclosure/copy conventions. IA / nav placement and onboarding tooltips tracked in DES-189.

Primary users
- Platform / ML engineers optimizing inference cost for specific routes/models/regions.
- Internal CS/SE/TAMs using the view during onboarding and quarterly optimization reviews.

Non-goals (beta)
- No “Apply” / one-click changes (read-only). Apply workflows are phase 2.
- No deep “what-if” simulator beyond a simple before/after comparison row in the drawer.

Design artifacts
- Confluence UX spec (canonical): sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-suggestions-view-ux-spec.json
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/optimization-suggestions-console-ux-beta-prd.json
- Risk taxonomy reference: ADR-0274
- Savings contract reference: ADR-0275

Information architecture (in-scope portion)
- Page: Console → Optimize → Suggestions (beta)
- Two-pane pattern via a right-side detail drawer; list remains visible underneath for easy triage.

Suggestions list (table) — proposed structure
Table columns (default, v1)
1) Suggestion (title + short subtitle)
   - Example title: “Increase continuous batching window” / “Enable prefix caching for /chat/completions”
   - Subtitle includes scope chips: route/model/region (truncate with +N)
2) Risk (chip)
   - Low / Medium / High
   - Color: use existing severity tokens, but do NOT use “error red” for High (avoid implying incident). Use “warning” palette.
3) Estimated savings
   - Display primary metric as “$ / 1M tokens” delta (e.g., “Save ~$12–$18 / 1M tokens”)
   - Secondary line: “≈ $X–$Y / mo” (based on last 7d/30d baseline; see disclosure)
4) Confidence (beta decision)
   - Decision: do NOT add a separate confidence column in list for beta. Confidence is shown in drawer as part of “Basis of estimate,” and uncertainty is represented by ranges in the savings display.
   - Rationale: avoid cognitive overload + avoid users interpreting confidence as a guarantee; reduce “why is risk high vs confidence low” confusion.
5) Updated
   - Relative (e.g., “3h ago”, “2d ago”); hover shows exact timestamp.

Row interactions
- Click row → open detail drawer.
- Multi-select deferred (no bulk actions in beta).

List controls
- Search: free-text across route/model/suggestion title.
- Filters (multi-select where applicable):
  - Route
  - Model
  - Region
  - Suggestion type (Caching | Batching)
  - Risk level (Low | Medium | High)
- Sort:
  - Recommended default sort: “Highest estimated monthly savings”
  - Alternate: Risk (Low→High), Updated (newest)

Pagination
- Use cursor-based pagination (Console standard). Provide “Load more” pattern rather than page numbers if implementation prefers; either acceptable as long as state is preserved when drawer opens.

Empty + error states (must-have)
1) No suggestions available
   - Copy: “No suggestions right now” + “We’ll surface opportunities when we have enough recent traffic and telemetry.”
   - CTA: link to docs “Why am I not seeing suggestions?”
2) Insufficient telemetry
   - Copy must be explicit: “Insufficient recent telemetry to estimate savings for this scope.”
   - Provide “What’s required” bullets (token metering, request volume threshold, last updated window).
3) Feature gated / allowlist
   - If user not enabled: show a neutral gated state (no broken experience).
4) API/service error
   - Provide retry button + request id.

Detail drawer — content hierarchy
Header
- Suggestion title
- Scope line (route/model/region). If multiple, show “Applies to: 3 routes, 2 models, us-east-1” with an expandable list.
- Badges: Risk chip + Suggestion type chip

Section 1: Summary (“What we recommend”)
- 2–3 bullets maximum.
- Must include the actionable change at a human level (even though beta is read-only):
  - Example: “Increase max batch size from 8 → 16 for route /v1/chat”
  - Example: “Enable prefix caching for requests with stable system prompts”
- Include reversibility note (important for trust): “Reversible: Yes (configuration-only).” (If not reversible, call out explicitly; most of these should be reversible in beta.)

Section 2: Savings (disclosure-first, not promise)
- Primary callout: “Estimated savings” with range:
  - “Save ~$12–$18 / 1M tokens”
  - “≈ $2.1k–$3.2k / month (based on last 30 days)”
- Before/after comparison (simple, v1)
  - Two-column mini table:
    - Current: “$X / 1M tokens”
    - Estimated after: “$Y / 1M tokens”
  - If only partial data: degrade gracefully to show only the metric we trust.
- Important: avoid precision. Use rounded values and ranges.

Section 3: Risk (make “High” actionable)
- Display: Risk chip + one sentence definition (from ADR-0274)
- “Why this is the risk level” (rationale bullets)
  - Minimum 2 bullets; max 5.
  - Examples of acceptable rationale bullets:
    - “Latency headroom is <10% at p95 during peak hours.”
    - “Workload variance is high (p95 tokens/request fluctuates 3× week-over-week).”
    - “Cache hit-rate estimate is based on <N samples; may not generalize.”
- “What could change” (impact areas)
  - Explicitly list potential impacts: latency p95, throughput, tail spikes, quality risk (if any).
  - If quality risk is “not expected,” say so but avoid absolutes: “No quality changes expected (configuration does not alter model), but downstream timeouts may affect user experience.”

Section 4: Basis of estimate (trust + troubleshooting)
- “Data window”: last 7d/30d used
- “Last computed”: timestamp
- “Inputs used” (non-sensitive, aggregated)
  - request volume bucket
  - avg/p95 tokens/request bucket
  - current cache hit-rate (if applicable) as a range
  - current batch utilization (if applicable)
- “Assumptions” bullets
  - Example: “Traffic mix remains similar to last 30d.”
  - Example: “No change in model version.”
- Link to docs for methodology (internal beta doc; external-facing docs for GA).

Footer
- For beta: “Share feedback” link (opens an internal form / mailto alias for cohort) + “Copy suggestion ID” for support.

Copy guidelines (beta)
- Always use “Estimated” savings; never “Guaranteed.”
- Use “may”/“could” for impacts; do not imply Redwood will apply changes.
- Provide ranges and “based on last X days” wherever a number is shown.

Design system / accessibility notes
- Risk chips must meet contrast; ensure not color-only (include text).
- Drawer must be keyboard navigable; focus trap; ESC to close.
- Table density: default comfortable; allow compact density as a future enhancement (not in beta).

Open questions resolved in this ticket
1) Confidence vs risk
- Resolved: no separate confidence column in list for beta; represent uncertainty via ranges + basis section.
- Reason: reduces confusion and aligns with #product feedback that risk should remain the primary “should I touch this?” signal.

2) Where to place risk chip
- Resolved: show risk in list as its own column + again in drawer header.
- Reason: users triage based on risk before clicking; duplication is acceptable.

3) “Insufficient data” handling
- Resolved: show Suggestions page but with explicit empty state; do not hide nav item.
- Reason: prevents “is this broken?” support tickets; aligns with beta expectations.

Acceptance criteria
- List view supports search + filters (route/model/region/type/risk) and sorting.
- Clicking a suggestion opens a drawer with:
  - summary of recommended change
  - savings with range + before/after
  - risk level + rationale bullets
  - basis of estimate (data window, last computed, assumptions)
- Empty states for: no suggestions, insufficient telemetry, gated/allowlist.
- Copy adheres to “estimated” language and avoids overpromising.

Implementation handoff notes (for ENG-2404)
- Drawer content is driven by API fields; ensure we have:
  - risk_level + rationale[] + assumptions[]
  - savings_range_min/max per 1M tokens + monthly min/max + baseline window
  - last_computed_at timestamp
- Suggestion “scope” must handle multiple routes/models/regions; plan for truncation + expandable list.

Links / references
- Linear: ENG-2404 (UI implementation), ENG-2402 (API list/detail), ENG-2410 (schema versioning)
- GitHub: redwood#18680 (list page), redwood#18681 (detail drawer)
- Slack: #design thread 1709654421 (risk chip placement + drawer hierarchy)
- Support feedback reference: SUP-19402 (“High risk is too vague” → rationale bullets added)

Updates
2026-01-11 (Kenji)
- Drafted list table columns + drawer hierarchy. Proposed risk column + savings range formatting.

2026-01-18 (Tessa)
- Design review: agreed on two-pane drawer pattern; remove confidence column for beta; add “Basis of estimate” section to prevent trust issues.

2026-01-26 (Alicia)
- Iterated empty states: explicit “insufficient telemetry” variant + docs link. Added “Copy suggestion ID” affordance for support.

2026-02-04 (Kenji)
- Final spec delivered to engineering; aligned with ADR-0274/0275 language. Confirmed accessibility requirements (keyboard, focus trap).

2026-02-14 (Kenji)
- Marking Done: engineering implemented list + drawer consistent with spec (redwood#18680, #18681). Remaining IA/onboarding polish tracked in DES-189.
